policy: Defensive post-mortem metadata only. No payloads, no private keys, no unpublished 0-days. Sources are public writeups from Rekt, Immunefi, protocol teams, audit firms, and contest reports.

incidents.name: Euler Finance donateToReserves
incidents.summary: eIP-14 added donateToReserves without the account-health check every other balance path used. An attacker flash-loaned, looped eToken/dToken, donated collateral to reserves (debt unchanged), then self-liquidated at a discount.
incidents.lesson: Every path that reduces collateral or equity must run the same solvency check as withdraw/borrow/liquidate. A 'donation' is still a balance mutation.

incidents.name: KyberSwap Elastic tick double-count
incidents.summary: When sqrtP sat exactly on a tick boundary, liquidity was added both to baseL and again when the tick was crossed. A flash-loaned multi-tick swap drained concentrated-liquidity pools.
incidents.lesson: CLAMM invariants must hold on the exact tick, not only strictly inside a range. Fuzz getTickAtSqrtRatio / nextSqrtP equality.

incidents.name: Curve Vyper compiler reentrancy
incidents.summary: Vyper 0.2.15–0.3.0 emitted a broken @nonreentrant lock. Factory pools compiled with those versions were re-entered during add_liquidity.
incidents.lesson: Pin compiler versions against public advisories. A source-level lock is not a lock if the compiler is wrong.

incidents.name: Prisma MigrateTroveZap flash-loan callback
incidents.summary: onFlashloan() on a migration zap accepted attacker-chosen trove parameters. Users who had approved the zap lost collateral; the zap reopened their trove with less collateral.
incidents.lesson: Callbacks are public ABI. Bind caller, initiator, and the exact encoded action. Zap approvals are standing authorities.

incidents.name: Penpie permissionless market + harvest reentrancy
incidents.summary: Anyone could register a Pendle-style market. A fake SY token re-entered _harvestBatchMarketRewards, which measured rewards as a balance delta and had no reentrancy lock.
incidents.lesson: Do not treat permissionless registries as trusted oracles. Reward = after-before is unsafe if the callee can re-enter and deposit.

incidents.name: Radiant Capital signer-device compromise
incidents.summary: A live lending market was drained after developer devices were malware-compromised and the multisig threshold was met. Not a Solidity bug; an operational-security failure.
incidents.lesson: On-chain 'multisig' is only as strong as key custody, hardware isolation, and delayed execution. Documented multisig is not a proof.

incidents.name: Cetus Protocol spoof-token pricing (Sui)
incidents.summary: Spoof tokens with negligible liquidity were introduced into Cetus pricing/reserve logic, moving internal curves and draining real reserves.
incidents.lesson: Price and reserve accounting must reject unknown or illiquid objects. Object-centric chains still need allowlists and liquidity floors.

incidents.name: Wormhole guardian signature bypass
incidents.summary: A deprecated verification path accepted a crafted secp256k1 signature and minted 120k wETH without guardian quorum.
incidents.lesson: Deprecated syscalls and leftover verify paths are live attack surface. Bind the current verifier and fail closed.

incidents.name: Ronin 5-of-9 validator compromise
incidents.summary: A 5-of-9 validator set was effectively one operator plus a partner. Social engineering collected the threshold.
incidents.lesson: Count distinct custodians, not validator slots. Threshold math is meaningless if keys share an org.

incidents.name: Nomad zero trusted root
incidents.summary: A replica was initialized so the default bytes32(0) looked like a proven message. Anyone could process arbitrary messages.
incidents.lesson: Uninitialized mappings equal zero. Zero must never be a valid root, message, or owner.

incidents.name: Beanstalk flash-loan governance
incidents.summary: Live BEAN balances were voting power and execution had no delay. A flash-loaned BIP drained the treasury.
incidents.lesson: Snapshot votes at a past block and timelock execution. Emergency pause should not be flash-votable.

incidents.name: Harvest Finance Curve spot share price
incidents.summary: Vault share price was a same-tx Curve virtual price. Flash dump, deposit expensive shares, withdraw, restore.
incidents.lesson: Share price cannot be a single-block AMM read. Use TWAP, independent oracles, or sandwich-resistant valuation.

incidents.name: Mango Markets oracle / MNGO spot
incidents.summary: Thin MNGO spot was moved, inflated borrow power, and drained the protocol. Legal/market-manipulation debate followed; the code trusted a manipulable price.
incidents.lesson: Collateral listing requires depth, TWAP windows, and open-interest caps. A listed token is not a safe oracle.

incidents.name: Wintermute Profanity / proxy takeover
incidents.summary: A vanity-address generator leaked private-key bits. Combined with proxy/admin assumptions this enabled a large drain.
incidents.lesson: Vanity address tools and uninitialized admin slots are in scope. Review key-generation as well as Solidity.

incidents.name: Compound Comptroller reward scale
incidents.summary: A proposal shipped a 1e36 vs 1e18 scale error and over-distributed COMP. Audited code plus governance still shipped it.
incidents.lesson: Invariant-test reward index math at the unit-test level. Governance review is not a substitute for a scale-factor check.

incidents.name: Poly Network hash-then-substitute
incidents.summary: A header was verified, then a different body field was executed. Cross-chain auth hashed one thing and acted on another.
incidents.lesson: The bytes that are signed must be the bytes that are executed. No post-verify substitution.

incidents.name: Cashio infinite mint via fake collateral
incidents.summary: Saber LP collateral accounts were not bound to the expected mint/program. A fake account printed CASH.
incidents.lesson: Every AccountInfo that influences mint/burn must be typed, owned, and mint-constrained.

incidents.name: Sherlock/C4 first-depositor class (2024-2025 contests)
incidents.summary: Pareto, BakerFi, Burve and many other contest vaults still shipped ERC-4626 share math without virtual offsets. Attackers donate, victims mint zero shares.
incidents.lesson: This class is not theoretical. Default OZ ERC4626 offsets or burned dead shares are mandatory.

incidents.name: Immunefi 2025: protocol-logic now dominates losses
incidents.summary: Immunefi reported DeFi losses of $680.3M in 2025. Bridge share of losses fell to ~3%. Flash-loan-as-primary-vector is now <1%. Protocol-specific business logic was ~89% of remaining DeFi losses.
incidents.lesson: Generic reentrancy/oracle scanners are table stakes. The remaining risk is invariant and integration review — which is why SELF autonomous exists.

incidents.name: Lendf.Me ERC777 tokensToSend
incidents.summary: A Compound fork accepted ERC777. tokensToSend re-entered supply() before accounting settled.
incidents.lesson: Token standards are callbacks. Assume transfer/transferFrom can re-enter unless the token is allowlisted and hook-free.
